Joburg Property Company

By: Joy Summers | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
The EFF call her their force, their centre of power in the city of Johannesburg. For 14 years Helen Botes has been at the helm of the Johannesburg Property company, doing deals and allegedly dishing o

Unique Selling Point:
Two insiders who have intimate knowledge of the JPC willing to do interviews and documents to back up their story

Summary:
In September 2022 the new board thought they had a watertight case against her and she was about to be suspended. But instead her political guardians turned the tables on the boards and the coalition government and ousted them. So Helen Botes remains the JPC property company and her protectors remain in charge of the city.

A former politician in the city tells Carte Blanche:

I was told confidentially by the EFF, they call her our force. They said we got paid to vote with the ANC. You will never find the ANC working with the EFF but in this instance against instructions from the ANC at national level, they coalesced at this level. “She is the ANC and EFF kingpin, If she loses her job they will probably take her out, because she has something on everyone.” She is rumoured to have a wine farm and a Rolls Royce and has managed to outplay her enemies for 14 years

Now in a Carte Blanche exclusive we speak on camera to the former chairperson of the JPC board, an advocate who tells the story of how they tried to hold Botes to account but were played because they were trying to fight the battles legally -not understanding the extent of the political network they were targeting.

“the calibre of the people who were in that board you will never get it again, and it was the first time that woman was held accountable!


Further information:
TECHNICALLY INSOLVENT
The JPC is technically bankrupt, there is no proper audit of the properties, and instead of the city making revenue from the properties it owns, the funds are being diverted to politically connected individuals.

“When you go deeper into the books you don’t get the answers. We know as a board that they are technically insolvent. Even the cleaners in the city are contracted by JPC so that cost is very high. We don’t know they made that decision, and then they buy mops almost every week. You can see these guys are ripping it.


PROTON HOUSE
The JPC leases buildings from private companies for their staff, and it’s in these transactions our sources say corruption happens. Proton house, a building in Constantia Kloof was leased from 2017 to 2019 to the city for around R500 000 per year from a company called Bertocure. The only director of Bertocure Herbert Theledi - apparently politically connected. ( We have documents on this transaction) The city moved out in 2019 but payments were still made to Bertocure. Then Bertocure demanded the city paid over R27 million to reinstate the building to its original state and JPC paid the R27 million rand without any agreements and hid the payment from the board. It’s this transaction that the former board chair says was fraudulent and was the watertight case. The Hawks are looking into this transaction and can show anomalies in the bank account. We have the bank account numbers but not names ( don’t know how to get those) that may suggest that payments were made out of this account to various cadres.

DOCUMENTS
We have obtained all the documentation which backs up the story and have the names of those in the political network that protects her.

PART OF THE NETWORK

DADO MORERO GAUTENG CHAIR OF THE ANC.
Our source says HB has very close ties with Dado Morero the Joburg ANC chair. Morero’ wife works at JPC as a project manager. One of her projects is the Rissik street post office. But she is there to look after Dado’s money. His money comes from the JPC and it funded his campaign. He is the engineer behind everything - he has an official position in the ANC but I don’t think anyone is more powerful than this woman. She has files upon files on everyone, that is why they leave her alone.

FLOYD BRINK
Helen Botes and city manager Floyd Brink are very close. Floyd comes from Limpopo and he is the EFF’s guy. He kept the SIU report on the PPE in his draw and the SIU had made recommendations to the city on Botes but nothing happened

THE DA has a case against JPC - still need to investigate how this overlaps.

CLOSING DOWN GFIS.
Group Forensic services began an investigation into JPC, but it’s been blocked and gone nowhere, and now the current administration is trying to get rid of GFIS. We can try and speak to the former acting head of GFIS who was pushed out.

THE HAWKS
The Hawks are also apparently investigating and have traced payments from Bertocure to various accounts that appear to be irregular.

JPC FINAL SCRIPT FOR TX 8th OCTOBER 2023

Voice over 1
A shadow has fallen over Johannesburg.

A patronage network is sucking it dry.

Insiders say there’s a protection ring of politicians and officials, and those who take them on… don’t last.


Look at the Johannesburg Property Company, the JPC, they said, the private company that manages the city’s portfolio of thousands of properties

From hostels to sports clubs, museums and offices... it’s easy to make money disappear at the JPC.

Its CEO is Helen Botes. She has been in charge for 14 years. Her current annual salary - R3,4 million, with a R413 000 performance bonus and R250 000 to travel the world

But an insider says Botes is at the centre of a network that has channelled city cash to politicians. In return they protect her

MR X
She has mastered the art of dispensing patronage. She has mastered the art of paying people. And how they do it is through the property portfolio

Voice over 2
The JPC manages the city’s portfolio of 27 908 properties, valued they say, at around R9 billion rand. Its priorities are to maximise revenue to make the city a better place, to keep an updated asset register of those properties, and to control and bill outdoor advertising.
In Feb last year, advocate Brenda Madumise was elected chairperson of JPC’s new board, to which the CEO is answerable.

Brenda Madumise Pajibo Former board chair: JPC
And that is what we came in to do, just to hold management and executives accountable.

Voice over 3
Her board had questions for Botes, but found they seldom got satisfactory answers.

Brenda
She believed that no- one can challenge her or test her, because she's got the answers, because she's been there for 14 years. You just came in, you think you know. You don't know. I know, and I know better than all of you. And I'll give you the answers.
Govan
In your case, you interrogated them.
Yeah.
And frequently, right?
Brenda: Many times

Voice over 4
Advocate Madumise hasn’t given a television interview on what she found behind the scenes at JPC last year. Until now.

Beat 1, Beat 2

It’s alleged that under Botes, the JPC was enmeshed in a bitter political power play in the corridors of City Hall.

Brenda
And I saw how politics play themselves out in this city. You will compromise service delivery to your residents who pay huge sums of money to keep this city going, and not have a conscience. None whatsoever.

Up sound: Executive mayor and clapping.

Voice over 5
At the time the DA mayor, Mpho Phalatse, led a fragile coalition of ten different parties.

Up sound Mpho Palatse
I am really excited, I am encouraged by the passion we have all shown for our beloved city.

Voice over 5 B
But the ANC was champing at the bit to take control of Johannesburg again.

Beat, Beat
Advocate Madumise, though, was focussed on the JPC’s finances. She worried that revenue from their leases wasn’t what it should be.

Brenda
So if you look at the property portfolio, when they give you the statements from finance and you look at how much they're collecting, it's shocking what they are collecting.

Voice over 6
The JPC’S recent financials confirm a company that is technically insolvent. By far its biggest expense at around R465 million rand, is salaries. The company is only kept going by a grant it gets from government.

Former Mayoral Committee member for Economic Development, Leah Knott, says that’s despite the JPC earning money from leases and outdoor advertising.

Leah Knott
Well, all commercial contracts, the big ones, the million rand contracts that adorn our streets and city of Joburg properties, JPC manages those contracts, but if you had to go look at their books, they hardly have any viable or current contracts that are actually bringing revenue into the city. But somebody is receiving revenue because they're getting the permissions and the authorization to put these up.

Voice over 7
But ailing finances - despite an impressive property and advertising portfolio - are not where the controversy around the JPC ends.

LINK
The city also leases hundreds of buildings from private landlords for their departments, and spends millions every month paying rent.

Voice over 8
Last year JPC paid out R140 million rand.

Govan
Why does JPC lease properties from private property owners when it has so many properties of its own?
Brenda
Good question. I think it's a model that works and makes money for many people.

Voice over 9
Then last year, this building- Proton house, leased to the city from 2017 to 2019, became the centre of a scandal, that might just provide an insight into the underbelly of dirty politics in Johannesburg

Leah Knott
That building, if you've ever visited it and I did, and it was decrepit. The lifts didn't work, the doors were broken. You know, some of the disabled staff actually couldn't get into the building. It was rundown when the city rented it, so a year ago we had already moved our staff out because of the safety issues.

Voice over 10
Months later, the landlord demanded that JPC pay R27 million rand to restore the building to what it was. A city report put the amount at closer to R2 million rand.

It seemed the landlord was adding costs that were not for a tenant.

Leah Knott
All of a sudden now we need to pay the owner of Proton House R27 million rand to bring the property back to the state it was before.

Voice over 11
A figure that high needed the approval of the JPC board. But, Brenda alleges Botes altered what’s known as a “delegation of authority” allowing her to push the payment through. The board was none the wiser.

Brenda Madumise
We realised that we approved this particular document and certain clauses were changed.
Govan
By who?
Brenda
By her! After the fact, right? So you delete a section.

Voice over 12
By that time the board had already held several meetings, including one in which the JPC informed them of a R700 000 sponsorship deal… making the secrecy around the Proton House payment even more baffling.

Brenda
And here's what boggled the mind and that of the entire board. So inform us for R700,00 but you didn't see it fit to tell this board that we have paid out R27 million

Voice over 13
Brenda’s board was about to suspend Botes. They had 8 charges against her including a failure to act with fidelity and honesty and in the best interests of the JPC.

Brenda
There were very serious charges, and we are very confident in our pursuit of all of that.
Govan
You mean you were confident you could prove that she had committed fraud?
Brenda
Yeah, we could. And I'm still very confident till today.

Voice over 14
And it's here that greed, politics, and the alleged rot at the JPC collide. According to our insider, Botes mustered her political forces to ensure she stayed in her position, re-routing the R27 million from Proton house to buy the allegiance of councillors and the EFF.

MR X
They call her our force. They say she is our force.

Voice over 15
And says our insider, she was a force for the ANC, too.



Mr X
Because if you don't change government, she is gone and therefore there is no longer a channel for patronage for the ANC in the long term to raise funds for the elections in 2024.
Govan
Are you saying that the money from Proton House, the R27 million, was used to change the government in the city of Johannesburg?
MR X
Yes, definitely. Definitely. An illegal decision was taken to serve a motion of no confidence the following day
Govan
On the day they would suspend Helen Botes?
MR X
On the day she was going to be suspended. They acted like gangsters, it was like hunters seeing blood. And they did it anyway so that they can quickly arrest the situation and prevent Helen Botes from being fired.

Voice over 16
Former DA Mayor Mpho Phalatse laid charges soon after.
UP Sound Mpho Phalatse
“Part of that R27 million would be used to destabilise the coalition government by funding the payment of bribes...

Voice over 17
Phalatse also alleged that the Proton house payment was used to buy votes to collapse her administration. Botes called it theatrics and denied any wrongdoing.

Leah Knott
There were other individuals who also claim to have seen, you know, sort of it sounds like a movie, money in boots of cars being exchanged in the basement just before this vote happened
Govan
But is she such a big political player that she could change the government in the city of Johannesburg to ensure she doesn't lose her position?
Leah Knott
It sounds bizarre and it sounds unrealistic, but my experience with it is that every time you have evidence against her, it disappears or it gets swept under the carpet. But ja, it's highly coincidental that all of these things happened around the same time.

Voice over 18
Soon after, the JPC board received a letter from their new political bosses: All decisions taken by the boards in September 2022 were revoked.

Brenda
Remember the decisions that we made in September were the appointed forensic investigators, also to institute this very difficult process against the CEO. Why would you tell us to stop what we're doing? What is the justification for you instructing this board not to do its work?

Voice over 19
Botes’s disciplinary was swept away, and not long after so was Brenda’s board. Botes had won.

Brenda
I mean, in this case the union was fighting for Helen! They fought for her! They accused us, called us names. They wrote us letters demanding our resignation, that's the order of the day, you will be hounded out.
Govan
It seems like going up against Helen Botes is
hopeless. That she's unbeatable?
Brenda
I think so too, right? I think if you want to have your
career and be okay, maintain peace, stay away from trying to challenge certain individuals. Stay away from raising issues because you'll be persona non grata!

LINK
At the height of Covid the JHB property went on a spending spree. In one day they spent R7 million here fogging the basement parking 7 times. When the SIU took a closer look they implicated Helen Botes. Now just a few floors up in the city manager's office - that report is gathering dust

Voice over 21
If anyone was able to ensure action was taken on the allegations against Botes, its City Manager Floyd Brink, appointed earlier this year. But he too has failed to act, despite the Special Investigation Unit recommending both disciplinary and criminal referrals

Mr X.
It has been over two years. Nothing has ever happened. So you ask yourself, is it the incompetence on the part of our law enforcement, or is it somebody who is one step ahead, who is able to cover the bases ahead of time and have the ability to kill the cases before they happen?

Voice over 22
But it wasn’t just the SIU that had looked into Botes.
Group Forensics or GFIS, who investigate corruption by city officials, also had evidence of wrongdoing under her watch.

Contractors had overcharged JPC, submitted fake invoices, or not done the work at all.

Govan
What happened to GFIS investigations?
Brenda
Nothing. Nothing happened. So it is the paper that you will have before you, you are raising it today, six months along, someone else is going to raise it and it continues, right, because no one is going to be held accountable.

Voice over 23
Our insider says Brink protects Botes. But in a note to Carte Blanche, Brink has denied that.

Knott, though, questions why the current administration is actively shutting down the investigations, dismantling GFIS and taking control of who will be investigated.

Leah Knott
With Helen, you know, we've got the SIU investigations, we've got the GFIS investigations. At the moment we are fighting the disempowerment of GFIS, which is directly linked to the investigations that are being done into her, as well as several other high ranking officials within the administration.

Voice over 24
And the SIU’S criminal referral on Botes is with the National Prosecuting Authority

And now, Dada Morero, an ANC councilor appointed to the city’s key finance portfolio, has announced a R2 billion rand refurbishment of the Metro Centre. A project that falls within the ambit of the Johannesburg Property Company.

Govan
So you think the board was defeated by a patronage network?
Brenda
No doubt about it! No doubt about it! I mean, even me being here, it's going to make it worse, right? But, you know, who cares?

Voice over 25
The EFF and the ANC, ignored our request for an interview and so did Botes for over a month. On Friday afternoon she finally responded through the city spokesperson.

THE END

PROMO ONE
Voice over
The Johannesburg property company administers thousands of properties on behalf of the city
Brenda
So if you look at the property portfolio, when they give you the statements from finance, it's shocking what they are collecting.
Voice over
Formed to make the city a better place, a more sinister picture is emerging at the JPC

PROMO TWO
Voice over
Is the Johannesburg property company playing politics instead of looking after city assets?
Brenda
And I saw how politics play themselves out in this city.You will compromise service delivery to your residents who pay huge sums of money to keep this city going, and not have a conscience. None whatsoever.

PROMO THREE
In 2022 the DA led a fragile coalition in the Johannesburg city council. But what happened behind closed doors, when they were voted out last year.

Leah Knott
There were other individuals who also claim to have seen, you know, sort of it sounds like a movie, money in boots of cars being exchanged in the basement just before this vote happened


Maybe use for promo but taken out now
The company's act demands directors have integrity, honesty, competency and trust. Hard to find at the JPC

Carte Blanche HD nombuso@carteblanche.co.za 08 October 2023 TX Date: 0000-00-00 Script: JPC FINAL SCRIPT FOR TX 8th OCTOBER 2023 Voice over 1 A shadow has fallen over Johannesburg. A patronage network is sucking it dry. Insiders say there’s a protection ring of politicians and officials, and those who take them on… don’t last. Look at the Johannesburg Property Company, the JPC, they said, the private company that manages the city’s portfolio of thousands of properties From hostels to sports clubs, museums and offices... it’s easy to make money disappear at the JPC. Its CEO is Helen Botes. She has been in charge for 14 years. Her current annual salary - R3,4 million, with a R413 000 performance bonus and R250 000 to travel the world But an insider says Botes is at the centre of a network that has channelled city cash to politicians. In return they protect her MR X She has mastered the art of dispensing patronage. She has mastered the art of paying people. And how they do it is through the property portfolio Voice over 2 The JPC manages the city’s portfolio of 27 908 properties, valued they say, at around R9 billion rand. Its priorities are to maximise revenue to make the city a better place, to keep an updated asset register of those properties, and to control and bill outdoor advertising. In Feb last year, advocate Brenda Madumise was elected chairperson of JPC’s new board, to which the CEO is answerable. Brenda Madumise Pajibo Former board chair: JPC And that is what we came in to do, just to hold management and executives accountable. Voice over 3 Her board had questions for Botes, but found they seldom got satisfactory answers. Brenda She believed that no- one can challenge her or test her, because she's got the answers, because she's been there for 14 years. You just came in, you think you know. You don't know. I know, and I know better than all of you. And I'll give you the answers. Govan In your case, you interrogated them. Yeah. And frequently, right? Brenda: Many times Voice over 4 Advocate Madumise hasn’t given a television interview on what she found behind the scenes at JPC last year. Until now. Beat 1, Beat 2 It’s alleged that under Botes, the JPC was enmeshed in a bitter political power play in the corridors of City Hall. Brenda And I saw how politics play themselves out in this city. You will compromise service delivery to your residents who pay huge sums of money to keep this city going, and not have a conscience. None whatsoever. Up sound: Executive mayor and clapping. Voice over 5 At the time the DA mayor, Mpho Phalatse, led a fragile coalition of ten different parties. Up sound Mpho Palatse I am really excited, I am encouraged by the passion we have all shown for our beloved city. Voice over 5 B But the ANC was champing at the bit to take control of Johannesburg again. Beat, Beat Advocate Madumise, though, was focussed on the JPC’s finances. She worried that revenue from their leases wasn’t what it should be. Brenda So if you look at the property portfolio, when they give you the statements from finance and you look at how much they're collecting, it's shocking what they are collecting. Voice over 6 The JPC’S recent financials confirm a company that is technically insolvent. By far its biggest expense at around R465 million rand, is salaries. The company is only kept going by a grant it gets from government. Former Mayoral Committee member for Economic Development, Leah Knott, says that’s despite the JPC earning money from leases and outdoor advertising. Leah Knott Well, all commercial contracts, the big ones, the million rand contracts that adorn our streets and city of Joburg properties, JPC manages those contracts, but if you had to go look at their books, they hardly have any viable or current contracts that are actually bringing revenue into the city. But somebody is receiving revenue because they're getting the permissions and the authorization to put these up. Voice over 7 But ailing finances - despite an impressive property and advertising portfolio - are not where the controversy around the JPC ends. LINK The city also leases hundreds of buildings from private landlords for their departments, and spends millions every month paying rent. Voice over 8 Last year JPC paid out R140 million rand. Govan Why does JPC lease properties from private property owners when it has so many properties of its own? Brenda Good question. I think it's a model that works and makes money for many people. Voice over 9 Then last year, this building- Proton house, leased to the city from 2017 to 2019, became the centre of a scandal, that might just provide an insight into the underbelly of dirty politics in Johannesburg Leah Knott That building, if you've ever visited it and I did, and it was decrepit. The lifts didn't work, the doors were broken. You know, some of the disabled staff actually couldn't get into the building. It was rundown when the city rented it, so a year ago we had already moved our staff out because of the safety issues. Voice over 10 Months later, the landlord demanded that JPC pay R27 million rand to restore the building to what it was. A city report put the amount at closer to R2 million rand. It seemed the landlord was adding costs that were not for a tenant. Leah Knott All of a sudden now we need to pay the owner of Proton House R27 million rand to bring the property back to the state it was before. Voice over 11 A figure that high needed the approval of the JPC board. But, Brenda alleges Botes altered what’s known as a “delegation of authority” allowing her to push the payment through. The board was none the wiser. Brenda Madumise We realised that we approved this particular document and certain clauses were changed. Govan By who? Brenda By her! After the fact, right? So you delete a section. Voice over 12 By that time the board had already held several meetings, including one in which the JPC informed them of a R700 000 sponsorship deal… making the secrecy around the Proton House payment even more baffling. Brenda And here's what boggled the mind and that of the entire board. So inform us for R700,00 but you didn't see it fit to tell this board that we have paid out R27 million Voice over 13 Brenda’s board was about to suspend Botes. They had 8 charges against her including a failure to act with fidelity and honesty and in the best interests of the JPC. Brenda There were very serious charges, and we are very confident in our pursuit of all of that. Govan You mean you were confident you could prove that she had committed fraud? Brenda Yeah, we could. And I'm still very confident till today. Voice over 14 And it's here that greed, politics, and the alleged rot at the JPC collide. According to our insider, Botes mustered her political forces to ensure she stayed in her position, re-routing the R27 million from Proton house to buy the allegiance of councillors and the EFF. MR X They call her our force. They say she is our force. Voice over 15 And says our insider, she was a force for the ANC, too. Mr X Because if you don't change government, she is gone and therefore there is no longer a channel for patronage for the ANC in the long term to raise funds for the elections in 2024. Govan Are you saying that the money from Proton House, the R27 million, was used to change the government in the city of Johannesburg? MR X Yes, definitely. Definitely. An illegal decision was taken to serve a motion of no confidence the following day Govan On the day they would suspend Helen Botes? MR X On the day she was going to be suspended. They acted like gangsters, it was like hunters seeing blood. And they did it anyway so that they can quickly arrest the situation and prevent Helen Botes from being fired. Voice over 16 Former DA Mayor Mpho Phalatse laid charges soon after. UP Sound Mpho Phalatse “Part of that R27 million would be used to destabilise the coalition government by funding the payment of bribes... Voice over 17 Phalatse also alleged that the Proton house payment was used to buy votes to collapse her administration. Botes called it theatrics and denied any wrongdoing. Leah Knott There were other individuals who also claim to have seen, you know, sort of it sounds like a movie, money in boots of cars being exchanged in the basement just before this vote happened Govan But is she such a big political player that she could change the government in the city of Johannesburg to ensure she doesn't lose her position? Leah Knott It sounds bizarre and it sounds unrealistic, but my experience with it is that every time you have evidence against her, it disappears or it gets swept under the carpet. But ja, it's highly coincidental that all of these things happened around the same time. Voice over 18 Soon after, the JPC board received a letter from their new political bosses: All decisions taken by the boards in September 2022 were revoked. Brenda Remember the decisions that we made in September were the appointed forensic investigators, also to institute this very difficult process against the CEO. Why would you tell us to stop what we're doing? What is the justification for you instructing this board not to do its work? Voice over 19 Botes’s disciplinary was swept away, and not long after so was Brenda’s board. Botes had won. Brenda I mean, in this case the union was fighting for Helen! They fought for her! They accused us, called us names. They wrote us letters demanding our resignation, that's the order of the day, you will be hounded out. Govan It seems like going up against Helen Botes is hopeless. That she's unbeatable? Brenda I think so too, right? I think if you want to have your career and be okay, maintain peace, stay away from trying to challenge certain individuals. Stay away from raising issues because you'll be persona non grata! LINK At the height of Covid the JHB property went on a spending spree. In one day they spent R7 million here fogging the basement parking 7 times. When the SIU took a closer look they implicated Helen Botes. Now just a few floors up in the city manager's office - that report is gathering dust Voice over 21 If anyone was able to ensure action was taken on the allegations against Botes, its City Manager Floyd Brink, appointed earlier this year. But he too has failed to act, despite the Special Investigation Unit recommending both disciplinary and criminal referrals Mr X. It has been over two years. Nothing has ever happened. So you ask yourself, is it the incompetence on the part of our law enforcement, or is it somebody who is one step ahead, who is able to cover the bases ahead of time and have the ability to kill the cases before they happen? Voice over 22 But it wasn’t just the SIU that had looked into Botes. Group Forensics or GFIS, who investigate corruption by city officials, also had evidence of wrongdoing under her watch. Contractors had overcharged JPC, submitted fake invoices, or not done the work at all. Govan What happened to GFIS investigations? Brenda Nothing. Nothing happened. So it is the paper that you will have before you, you are raising it today, six months along, someone else is going to raise it and it continues, right, because no one is going to be held accountable. Voice over 23 Our insider says Brink protects Botes. But in a note to Carte Blanche, Brink has denied that. Knott, though, questions why the current administration is actively shutting down the investigations, dismantling GFIS and taking control of who will be investigated. Leah Knott With Helen, you know, we've got the SIU investigations, we've got the GFIS investigations. At the moment we are fighting the disempowerment of GFIS, which is directly linked to the investigations that are being done into her, as well as several other high ranking officials within the administration. Voice over 24 And the SIU’S criminal referral on Botes is with the National Prosecuting Authority And now, Dada Morero, an ANC councilor appointed to the city’s key finance portfolio, has announced a R2 billion rand refurbishment of the Metro Centre. A project that falls within the ambit of the Johannesburg Property Company. Govan So you think the board was defeated by a patronage network? Brenda No doubt about it! No doubt about it! I mean, even me being here, it's going to make it worse, right? But, you know, who cares? Voice over 25 The EFF and the ANC, ignored our request for an interview and so did Botes for over a month. On Friday afternoon she finally responded through the city spokesperson. THE END PROMO ONE Voice over The Johannesburg property company administers thousands of properties on behalf of the city Brenda So if you look at the property portfolio, when they give you the statements from finance, it's shocking what they are collecting. Voice over Formed to make the city a better place, a more sinister picture is emerging at the JPC PROMO TWO Voice over Is the Johannesburg property company playing politics instead of looking after city assets? Brenda And I saw how politics play themselves out in this city.You will compromise service delivery to your residents who pay huge sums of money to keep this city going, and not have a conscience. None whatsoever. PROMO THREE In 2022 the DA led a fragile coalition in the Johannesburg city council. But what happened behind closed doors, when they were voted out last year. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): The EFF call her their force, their centre of power in the city of Johannesburg. For 14 years Helen Botes has been at the helm of the Johannesburg Property company, doing deals and allegedly dishing o
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Two insiders who have intimate knowledge of the JPC willing to do interviews and documents to back up their story
metadata.Summary: In September 2022 the new board thought they had a watertight case against her and she was about to be suspended. But instead her political guardians turned the tables on the boards and the coalition government and ousted them. So Helen Botes remains the JPC property company and her protectors remain in charge of the city. A former politician in the city tells Carte Blanche: I was told confidentially by the EFF, they call her our force. They said we got paid to vote with the ANC. You will never find the ANC working with the EFF but in this instance against instructions from the ANC at national level, they coalesced at this level. “She is the ANC and EFF kingpin, If she loses her job they will probably take her out, because she has something on everyone.” She is rumoured to have a wine farm and a Rolls Royce and has managed to outplay her enemies for 14 years Now in a Carte Blanche exclusive we speak on camera to the former chairperson of the JPC board, an advocate who tells the story of how they tried to hold Botes to account but were played because they were trying to fight the battles legally -not understanding the extent of the political network they were targeting. “the calibre of the people who were in that board you will never get it again, and it was the first time that woman was held accountable!
metadata.Further information: TECHNICALLY INSOLVENT The JPC is technically bankrupt, there is no proper audit of the properties, and instead of the city making revenue from the properties it owns, the funds are being diverted to politically connected individuals. “When you go deeper into the books you don’t get the answers. We know as a board that they are technically insolvent. Even the cleaners in the city are contracted by JPC so that cost is very high. We don’t know they made that decision, and then they buy mops almost every week. You can see these guys are ripping it. PROTON HOUSE The JPC leases buildings from private companies for their staff, and it’s in these transactions our sources say corruption happens. Proton house, a building in Constantia Kloof was leased from 2017 to 2019 to the city for around R500 000 per year from a company called Bertocure. The only director of Bertocure Herbert Theledi - apparently politically connected. ( We have documents on this transaction) The city moved out in 2019 but payments were still made to Bertocure. Then Bertocure demanded the city paid over R27 million to reinstate the building to its original state and JPC paid the R27 million rand without any agreements and hid the payment from the board. It’s this transaction that the former board chair says was fraudulent and was the watertight case. The Hawks are looking into this transaction and can show anomalies in the bank account. We have the bank account numbers but not names ( don’t know how to get those) that may suggest that payments were made out of this account to various cadres. DOCUMENTS We have obtained all the documentation which backs up the story and have the names of those in the political network that protects her. PART OF THE NETWORK DADO MORERO GAUTENG CHAIR OF THE ANC. Our source says HB has very close ties with Dado Morero the Joburg ANC chair. Morero’ wife works at JPC as a project manager. One of her projects is the Rissik street post office. But she is there to look after Dado’s money. His money comes from the JPC and it funded his campaign. He is the engineer behind everything - he has an official position in the ANC but I don’t think anyone is more powerful than this woman. She has files upon files on everyone, that is why they leave her alone. FLOYD BRINK Helen Botes and city manager Floyd Brink are very close. Floyd comes from Limpopo and he is the EFF’s guy. He kept the SIU report on the PPE in his draw and the SIU had made recommendations to the city on Botes but nothing happened THE DA has a case against JPC - still need to investigate how this overlaps. CLOSING DOWN GFIS. Group Forensic services began an investigation into JPC, but it’s been blocked and gone nowhere, and now the current administration is trying to get rid of GFIS. We can try and speak to the former acting head of GFIS who was pushed out. THE HAWKS The Hawks are also apparently investigating and have traced payments from Bertocure to various accounts that appear to be irregular.
